title: AntRep - Getting Started
subtitle: A plain-English walkthrough for athletes and coaches. Follow the short path for your role, then use the screen guide when you need it.
edition: Onboarding guide - athlete and coach portals

parts.title: 1. Welcome to AntRep
parts.intro: AntRep has two connected sides. Athletes train and record results. Coaches build plans, follow progress and communicate with athletes.

sections.title: Choose the side you need
body: Use the athlete portal when you are doing your own training. Use the coach portal when you are managing somebody else's training.
One login can have both roles. Settings lets you add the other role or switch between roles without making another account.

head: Portal
Open it
Use it for
rows: Today's workout, set logging, plans, coach contact and progress
Athletes, plan building, assignments, coaching and reports

sections.title: Sign in or practise first
steps: Open the portal you want.
Sign in, or choose Create account and enter your name, email and a password of at least 8 characters.
If AntRep asks you to confirm your email, open the link in your inbox, return to AntRep and tap I've confirmed it.
body2: In a development or demo setup, Explore the demo opens a ready-made practice workspace. Demo changes stay in that browser and do not affect a real account.

screenshots.name: auth-current
screenshots.caption: The real coach sign-in screen, including the ready-made demo accounts and the link back to the athlete portal.

sections.tip: If the demo button is not shown, the published app is set to real accounts only.

sections.title: Know when your work is saved
body: Set values are saved as you enter them. There is no separate Save workout button.
Plan editors and profile forms do have a Save button. Use it before leaving those screens.

parts.title: 2. Athlete - your first workout
parts.intro: This is the shortest useful route: get a plan, open today, record your sets and check the result.

sections.title: Step 1 - get something to train
body: A plan tells AntRep what belongs on each training day. You can sync a plan from a coach or build your own on the Plans tab.
No plan yet? That is okay. Home has Extra work, where you can record any exercise immediately.
steps: For a coach plan: get the coach's invite code, open Settings, enter it under Coaches and tap Link.
Open Plans. Under From your coach, tap Sync on the plan you want to follow.
For your own plan: open Plans, tap New, set the schedule, add exercises and save.

screenshots.name: athlete-plans-current
screenshots.caption: Real demo data on Plans: coach assignments and athlete-owned plans are kept separate.

sections.title: Step 2 - open Home
body: Home answers one question: what am I doing on this date? The date bar, today's plan and Extra work are all on the same screen.
Tap Another day when you want to do a different scheduled session today. Use the date arrows when you want to write up training on the date it actually happened.

screenshots.name: athlete-home-current
screenshots.caption: Alex's current Home screen: date controls, today's Push day and Extra work in one place.

sections.title: Step 3 - start the session
body: Tap Start now on the workout card, then choose the mode that matches what you are doing.

head: Choice
Choose it when
rows: You are training now and want the live timer
You are moving a different planned day to today
You are entering the workout afterwards and do not need a timer

screenshots.name: athlete-start-current
screenshots.caption: The real Start workout sheet over Alex's Push day. A timer is optional.

sections.title: Step 4 - record each set
steps: Tap the exercise row to open its logging card.
Use the minus and plus buttons, or tap a number and type the exact value. Decimals such as 52.5 are supported.
Tap Add set when you need another row.
Use the tick beside the exercise when it is finished.
body2: The fields fit the exercise: strength uses weight and reps, cardio uses distance and time, and timed work uses seconds. RPE means how hard the set felt; 8 means you probably had about two good reps left.

screenshots.name: athlete-logging-current
screenshots.caption: Real set data for Alex's flat bench press, including last time, target values, set rows, rest and save status.

sections.tip: An empty set row is not counted until you enter a value.

sections.title: Step 5 - finish and check it
body: If you started a timer, stop it when the workout is over. Your set data was already saved while you logged.
Open Progress to see the session in your totals. Use Plans to find the whole session, or Exercises to follow one movement over time.

sections.title: If you missed a day

head: What you mean
What to do
rows: Record what I did last Tuesday
Home > date bar > choose Tuesday > log it there
Home > Extra work > Log an exercise

sections.tip: A past-date entry is labelled as a late log, but it still belongs to that date in your history.

parts.title: 3. Athlete - screen guide
parts.intro: The six buttons at the bottom stay in the same order. Here is what each one is for.

screenshots.name: athlete-home-current
screenshots.caption: The athlete tab bar stays visible at the bottom: Home, Plans, Coach, Progress, Library and Settings.

head: Tab
Use it for
rows: Today's plan, timers, set logging, another day and extra work
Sync a coach plan, create your own, inspect running and past plans
Activity, check-ins, notes and trackers with a linked coach
Streak, XP, totals, trends, plans, training days and exercises
Save exercises and choose how each one should be logged
Profile goals, appearance, coach linking, guide and account switching

sections.title: Reading Progress
body: Overall includes everything you logged. Pick a plan chip to narrow the numbers below to that plan.
Overview gives the quick read. Plans groups complete sessions. Days compares repeating training days. Exercises follows individual movements.

screenshots.name: athlete-progress-current
screenshots.caption: Alex's real demo analytics: plan scope, streak, XP, weekly totals and the start of the trend view.

sections.tip: A flat or empty chart is normal with only one session. Trends become useful after you have repeated the work.

sections.title: Setting up the Library
body: Mine contains exercises you saved. Browse all searches the built-in catalogue.
The logging method saved in Mine is reused in plans and Extra work, so fix it here if an exercise asks for the wrong fields.

screenshots.name: athlete-library-current
screenshots.caption: The real Mine view shows Alex's saved exercises and their logging methods.

sections.title: Working with a coach
body: Link a coach in Settings with a one-time invite code. The Coach tab then shows your shared activity, weekly check-ins, coach notes and measurement trackers.
To stop the coaching relationship, use Unlink beside that coach in Settings.

screenshots.name: athlete-coach-current
screenshots.caption: Alex's Coach screen shows the shared activity and coaching tools after linking.

parts.title: 4. Coach - onboard an athlete
parts.intro: The normal coach workflow is invite, build, assign, review and respond.

sections.title: Step 1 - invite the athlete
steps: Open Athletes and create an invite code.
Send the code to the athlete.
Ask them to enter it in Settings > Coaches before it expires.
body2: Codes are single-use and normally expire after 30 minutes. Unclaimed codes remain visible on the Athletes screen.

screenshots.name: coach-athletes-current
screenshots.caption: Coach Sam's real demo roster, including a live invite code and linked athletes.

sections.title: Step 2 - build a reusable plan
steps: Open Plans and tap New.
Choose a weekly schedule or a repeating multi-day cycle, then set the plan dates.
Name each day, add exercises and set the target sets, reps, weight, rest, RPE and coaching notes.
Save the plan.
sections.tip: A plan can be assigned to several athletes. Editing the coach-owned plan updates what its followers receive.

screenshots.name: coach-plans-current
screenshots.caption: Coach Sam's plan library uses real assignments and plan counts from the demo workspace.

sections.title: Step 3 - assign and wait for Sync
steps: Open Athletes and choose the athlete.
Open Assign.
Tap Assign beside the plan.
body2: Waiting means the athlete has not accepted it yet. Synced means it is active in their portal. A finished assignment can be restarted by the coach.

screenshots.name: coach-assign-current
screenshots.caption: Alex's Assign view shows what is active, waiting or available to send.

sections.title: Step 4 - review the athlete
body: Overview shows this week's completion, useful flags, adherence, totals, records, today's work and recent sessions.
Progress opens the same analytics structure the athlete uses. Coaching contains shared activity, check-ins, coach notes and trackers.

screenshots.name: coach-athlete-current
screenshots.caption: Coach Sam's live overview of Alex: weekly completion, flags and recent work.

sections.title: Step 5 - export or import when needed
body: The share button on the athlete page exports an Excel workbook or a set-by-set CSV. The plus button imports past training from a spreadsheet.
Exports include sessions, individual sets, exercises, check-ins, trackers and coach notes.

screenshots.name: coach-export-current
screenshots.caption: The real export sheet lists both available report formats and the data they contain.

sections.title: My training is separate
body: My training uses your athlete profile. It does not mix your sessions with an athlete you coach.
If it is not enabled yet, AntRep offers to add the athlete role to the same account.

parts.intro: Use this section when you know the result you want but not the screen name.

Go here
rows: Athlete Home > date bar > choose the old date
Change the fields used to log an exercise

head: Word
What it means
rows: The schedule and exercise instructions you intend to follow
One recorded round of an exercise
Weight multiplied by repetitions, added together
Effort from 1 to 10; 8 is roughly two good reps left
How much of the planned training was actually completed
Training entered on a past date

sections.title: When something looks wrong
body: Nothing appears on Home: check that a plan is synced, active and has started. You can still use Extra work.
An exercise asks for the wrong values: edit its logging method in Library > Mine.
A chart is empty: log the exercise or session at least twice so AntRep has two points to compare.
A coach plan says Waiting: the athlete still needs to tap Sync on Plans.
An invite code fails: it may be expired or already used. Ask the coach to create a fresh one.
A real account is blocked after sign-up: confirm the email address, return to AntRep and tap I've confirmed it.
